sentences: Sam and I pat a mat.
nwf_note: No nonsense-word subtest at this lesson. 1 candidate spellings are legal here; every one of them is rejected because it is heard as a real word, a respelling or a letter name. The candidates and the reason for each are in rejected_pseudowords, which is examiner data and is never shown on the child's page.
supply_note: Lesson 7 teaches f /f/ and no real word containing f is legal here. The taught letters are a f m p s t; the only decodable f word in English is 'fat', which is on core_vocabulary.BLOCKED. The word bank therefore stocks zero f words at this lesson. This is a supply limit in the curriculum, not a writing failure — recorded rather than worked around. The /f/ sound is first assessable at Lesson 8.
instrument_claim: Decoding check on this lesson's taught sound. NOT a clean alternate form: below Lesson 13 the published Form A already spends every on-target word that exists, so some overlap is unavoidable and a child who practised at home may have met these words. Read the score as 'can they decode these taught patterns', not as an independent re-test. Decodability forbids apostrophes, so this text is written in uncontracted forms. A child who reads "can't" for "can not", "don't" for "do not" or "let's" for "let us" is reading for meaning and MUST NOT be scored an error.
